caption:
Oracle's latest round has cut over 1,000 roles in India, part of a global reduction approaching 6,000. Mid and senior levels took the hit.

Read the pattern. The people removed were not the least capable. They were the least visible to the people drawing up the list.

Competence is assumed at your level. Everyone on that spreadsheet was competent. What separates the retained from the released is whether decision-makers can name what you hold, in one sentence, without checking.

In command, a unit that cannot be accounted for is a unit at risk. The same logic runs a restructuring meeting.

So do the work now, while you still have the room. Speak early in meetings, not last. State your position once, clearly, and hold the silence after it. Make your name attach to outcomes, not effort.

Visibility is not self-promotion. It is being accounted for when the list gets written.
alt_text: A plain dark background with bold white text reading: "Competence was never the question. Visibility was." The Lumina Presence wordmark sits small at the bottom.

topic.title: Oracle's fresh India layoffs hit mid and senior roles
topic.angle: Lumina's audience is exactly the experienced mid-to-senior professional being cut first — not for lack of capability, but for lack of visibility to the decision-makers drawing up the list.
topic.why_now: The Oracle round began roughly two weeks ago, with over 1,000 Indian employees affected as part of a global round nearing 6,000, and it is still circulating in Indian tech and business media.

rationale: A stark text-only visual matches the caption's blunt, command-style delivery and keeps the focus on the single hard idea about visibility during layoffs.
